test_title: Platform Integration & Module Architecture Non-Regression Test

summary.conclusion: Integration testing cannot proceed. Critical backend initialization issue prevents service startup. This is a fundamental architectural problem with cross-module SQLAlchemy model relationships that must be resolved before any functional testing is possible.

critical_findings.title: SQLAlchemy Cross-Module Relationship Initialization Deadlock
critical_findings.description: The backend fails to start due to SQLAlchemy mapper configuration errors when handling relationships between models defined in different modules. The modular refactoring introduced a circular dependency in model initialization that prevents the application from starting.

root_cause_analysis.issue: SQLAlchemy's declarative ORM requires all related model classes to be loaded and configured before relationships can be validated. In the current architecture:
steps: 1. app/main.py imports anagrafica_italiana module (defines SoggettoAnagrafico model)
2. app/main.py imports immobili module, which imports its routes
3. immobili routes import Proprietario model, which references SoggettoAnagrafico with back_populates
4. SoggettoAnagrafico attempts to establish relationship to Proprietario, but:  - Proprietario.back_populates='proprietari' expects SoggettoAnagrafico to have a 'proprietari' relationship
5. Similar issue occurs with Affittuario and Tecnico models from affitti_lungo module
6. SQLAlchemy mapper configuration fails because all related classes must be available BEFORE relationship configuration
root_cause_analysis.technical_details: When Python first evaluates the SoggettoAnagrafico class definition with relationship() calls, SQLAlchemy immediately attempts to configure the relationship registry. If the target class (e.g., Proprietario) hasn't been imported yet, or if it declares a back_populates relationship that SoggettoAnagrafico doesn't have, the mapper configuration fails with: sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError: One or more mappers failed to initialize

critical_findings.error_log: sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError: Mapper 'Mapper[SoggettoAnagrafico(soggetti_anagrafici)]' has no property 'affittuari'. If this property was indicated from other mappers or configure events, ensure registry.configure() has been called.

detailed_issue_analysis.architecture_design: The modular refactoring split the monolith into 3 business modules: anagrafica_italiana, immobili, affitti_lungo. Each module has its own models, routes, and schemas. This is a good design.
detailed_issue_analysis.cross_module_dependency_problem: The problem occurs specifically at the intersection of two design patterns: (1) Modular architecture with cross-module model relationships, and (2) FastAPI/SQLAlchemy automatic model initialization. When module routes are imported, models are loaded, triggering SQLAlchemy relationship configuration before all related models have been imported.

sequence: affitti_lungo/models/affittuari.py: defines Affittuario(Base) with relationship to SoggettoAnagrafico
ERROR: SoggettoAnagrafico already imported, SQLAlchemy tries to configure Affittuario → SoggettoAnagrafico relationship
ERROR: SoggettoAnagrafico model definition doesn't have affittuari relationship property

detailed_issue_analysis.why_previous_monolith_worked: In the previous architecture, all models were likely in a single location and imported together, or relationship configuration was deferred/handled differently. The modular split exposed this timing issue.
detailed_issue_analysis.why_simple_fixes_dont_work: The problem isn't missing properties - it's that SQLAlchemy requires ALL models in a relationship chain to be fully loaded BEFORE ANY mapper is configured. With cross-module dependencies and lazy route imports, this is difficult to guarantee.

recommended_solutions.title: Implement Explicit Model Registry Initialization
recommended_solutions.description: Create a dedicated module that imports ALL models from ALL modules in explicit dependency order BEFORE routes are imported.
implementation_steps: Create app/models/__init__.py that imports all models in dependency order
Ensure it's imported FIRST in app/main.py before any routes
Call SQLAlchemy registry.configure() explicitly after all imports

recommended_solutions.title: Use SQLAlchemy 2.0+ Initialization Events
recommended_solutions.description: Use SQLAlchemy's event system to defer relationship configuration until all models are loaded.
implementation_details: Define relationships in configure event rather than class definition
Ensures all models are loaded before relationships are established

recommended_solutions.title: Refactor Module Structure to Defer Route Imports
recommended_solutions.description: Move route definitions outside of module __init__.py to prevent automatic model loading during module import.
implementation_details: Routes only imported in app/main.py after all models are loaded
Module __init__.py only exports manifest, not routes
Explicit app.include_router() calls in main.py after model initialization

recommended_solutions.title: Eliminate Back-Populates in Cross-Module Relationships
recommended_solutions.description: Remove bidirectional relationships across modules; use one-way foreign key relationships only.
recommended_solutions.tradeoff: Less convenient ORM usage but eliminates circular dependency issues

lessons_learned: Cross-module foreign key relationships in modular architectures require careful initialization sequencing
SQLAlchemy's declarative ORM eagerly configures relationships at class definition time, not import time
In modular systems, route imports often trigger model loading - this must be accounted for in architecture
Bidirectional back_populates relationships across modules create tight coupling and initialization ordering dependencies
Comprehensive startup integration tests are essential for catching initialization issues early
conclusion: The modular refactoring introduces a critical SQLAlchemy initialization issue that blocks all testing. The problem is architectural: cross-module relationships with bidirectional back_populates create circular dependencies in model initialization. The recommended fix is to implement explicit model registry initialization (FIX-1) that imports all models in dependency order before routes are loaded. Once this is resolved, full integration testing can proceed. The frontend appears to be functioning correctly based on initial checks.
